text: Tuai is a rural settlement and village situated around Lake Whakamarino in the Wairoa District of the Hawke's Bay Region on New Zealand's North Island. The local Tuai Power Station, opened in 1929 as part of the Waikaremoana power scheme, is located on the lake's shores and has been remotely controlled by Genesis Energy from Tokaanu power station since the early 2000s. Artist Doris Lusk painted the power station in 1948, describing it as a “gothic building in the middle of the wild hills.” Lake Whakamarino, also known as Tuai Lake, is popular with anglers and can be accessed by fly-fishers using small unanchored boats. Statistics New Zealand classifies Tuai as a rural settlement covering 21.99 km² (8.49 sq mi), with an estimated population of 230 as of June 2025, a population density of 10 people per km², and is part of the Maungataniwha-Raupunga statistical area. The 2023 census recorded a population of 222, an increase of 6 people (2.8%) from 2018 and 9 people (4.2%) from 2013; there were 108 males and 114 females in 87 dwellings. 1.4% of residents identified as LGBTIQ+. The median age was 32.4 years (compared to 38.1 years nationally), with 63 people (28.4%) under 15, 42 (18.9%) aged 15 to 29, 90 (40.5%) aged 30 to 64, and 30 (13.5%) aged 65 or older. Ethnicity data shows 25.7% European (Pākehā), 87.8% Māori, and 1.4% Pasifika; English was spoken by 94.6%, Māori by 54.1%, and other languages by 2.7%; 2.7% of people could not speak a language (e.g., too young to talk). The percentage of people born overseas was 6.8%, compared to 28.8% nationally. Religious affiliations included 20.3% Christian, 32.4% Māori religious beliefs, 1.4% New Age, and 1.4% other religions; 40.5% had no religion, and 6.8% did not answer the census question. Among those aged 15 and over, 24 (15.1%) held a bachelor's or higher degree, 99 (62.3%) had a post-high school certificate or diploma, and 45 (28.3%) held only high school qualifications. The median income was $31,200 (compared to $41,500 nationally), with 3 people (1.9%) earning over $100,000 (compared to 12.1% nationally); employment status showed 63 (39.6%) full-time, 21 (13.2%) part-time, and 12 (7.5%) unemployed. Te Kūhā Tārewa Marae and Te Poho o Hinekura or Ruapani meeting house serves the Tūhoe hapū of Ngāti Hinekura and the Ngāti Ruapani hapū of Ngāti Hinekura and Tuwai. In October 2020, the Government committed $1,949,075 from the Provincial Growth Fund to upgrade the marae and 23 other Ngāti Kahungunu marae, expected to create 164 jobs. Te Kura o Waikaremoana is a Year 1–8 co-educational state primary school, a decile 2 school with a roll of 27 as of October 2025. It was formed in 2005 by the merger of Tuai School, established by 1929, and Kokako School, established between 1896 and 1898.
